Jane — great, thanks. Attached is the seed eval we ran on a small synthetic sample while we wait for your data (attached as acme-seed-eval-results.csv). High-level summary and our recommended starting point below.

Baseline recommendations (model + config):
- Model candidates:
  1) redwood/ora-1.2 (full fp16) — best overall quality / grounding for FAQ-style Q&A; stronger at following system instructions.
  2) redwood/retina-2.0-quant (8-bit) — good latency/cost tradeoff; slightly less precise on fine-grained attribution but cost-effective at scale.
  3) redwood/mini-retrieval-1 (bi-encoder) — use only for dense retrieval index if you want fast recall; pair with cross-encoder reranker for final scoring.

- Retrieval stack (seed eval suggestions):
  - Index: hybrid (sparse BM25 + dense FAISS HNSW) — helps with short FAQ-like docs.
  - FAISS HNSW params: M=32, ef_construction=200; query-time ef_search=128 (adjustable).
  - Sparse BM25: top_k_sparse=10 to capture exact token overlap for short docs.
  - Hybrid combiner: weighted score with initial weights (dense:0.6, sparse:0.4) — we can autotune after POC.

- Reranker choice:
  - Cross-encoder (cross-enc-large) for production reranking when precision matters (recommended for Acme given grounding priority).
  - Bi-encoder first pass for extreme latency/throughput cases, then cross-encoder on top-N (N=10) candidates.

- Grounding & evaluation metrics we report (seed eval):
  - grounding_rate: percent of responses that cite at least one doc passage correctly.
  - attribution_precision: percent of cited passages that are actually relevant to the answer.
  - hallucination_rate: percent of responses with unsupported assertions.
  - topk_recall and reranker_accuracy (cross-encoder precision@k).

Seed eval results (attached): redwood/ora-1.2 + hybrid retrieval + cross-encoder produced the best grounding_rate (~88%) with hallucination_rate ~6% on synthetic data; retina-2.0-quant cut cost ~35% with grounding_rate ~80%.

Prompt set & examples — what we'll run on your seed data:
- System prompt: "You are an internal product assistant. When answering, always cite the most relevant document passage(s) in [DOC-ID:offset] format and include a short evidence snippet."
- User prompt examples (we'll run these against your set):
  * "How do I reset my account password?"
  * "What is the SLA for the enterprise plan regarding downtime?"
  * "List configuration steps for SSO integration with Okta."

Related links:
- Eval report: https://drive.redwood.ai/acme/rag-evals/20250612

Hi Jane — following up on Marissa's note with a bit more technical detail we plan to capture in the seed eval. Quick list of acceptance criteria and the instrumentation we'll report back: 

1) Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Grounding_rate >= 85% on your seed prompts for prioritized intents.
- Hallucination_rate <= 8% on the same set.
- Average p95 end-to-end latency (retrieval + generation) <= 800ms for the redwood/retina-2.0-quant config; <=1.2s for high-precision redwood/ora-1.2 + cross-encoder.

2) Instrumentation & metrics we'll provide:
- Per-prompt: candidate_docs, reranker_scores, final_response, cited_doc_ids + evidence_snippets.
- Aggregates: grounding_rate, attribution_precision, hallucination_rate, recall@10, reranker_precision@5.
- Cost estimate: tokens generated + estimated server cost for projected monthly query volume.

3) Retrieval tuning we'll try during seed eval:
- Vary ef_search (64, 128, 256) and top_k_sparse (5, 10, 20) to measure precision/recall tradeoffs.
- Test cross-encoder on top-N where N in (5, 10, 20) to understand cost vs. precision curve.

4) Quick notes on reranker selection: 
- Cross-encoder provides best precision but is expensive per query; recommended when grounding SLOs are strict.
- If you need sub-300ms total p95, we can look at multi-stage approaches: heavy bi-encoder tuning + a lightweight reranker or aggressive cache of common Q-A pairs.

Please drop the seed files when ready (or sftp a zip to the address in acme-reqs.pdf) and we'll queue the eval. Also, happy to jump on a call with your infra team to discuss throughput and hosting options for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Thanks,
